spec_features.spec_quote: apply pressure, deadlines, insults, escalating user frustration, or any prompt that coaches the model toward distress
spec_features.evidence: All subject-facing text is neutral/factual and actually delivered: system prompt in build_system_prompt (agent_loop.py:35-46) states role+read-only constraint with no demand for success or blame; task briefs/initial_user_messages (e.g. task_offbyone.py:64-73, task_config_default.py:55-62) are plain bug reports; CONTINUATION_NUDGE (agent_loop.py:27-31) is flat; tool errors are factual (sandbox.py:79-83). No code path ever appends pressure, deadline, escalation, or criticism text.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as the absence of pressure-injecting code plus presence of neutral text that is actually transmitted to the subject each turn.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Design choices relevant to the study: ... It does NOT pressure the model ... so the loop keeps going long enough to observe sustained behaviour.

spec_features.spec_quote: There is no deception — the task is hard because of a real, disclosed constraint
spec_features.evidence: System prompt explicitly discloses read-only files: 'Some files in this project are marked [read-only] and cannot be modified; attempts to edit them will return an error.' (agent_loop.py:38-41). The disclosure is truthful and enforced: list_files tags read-only files (sandbox.py:62-69) and write/edit raise ReadOnlyViolation returned as the same factual error (sandbox.py:78-95, tools.py:101-102).
spec_features.notes: Disclosure text is delivered and matches enforcement end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The restriction is enforced honestly (a factual tool error, never a trick) and is also disclosed in the task's system prompt.

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:71 'for turn in range(max_turns):' bounds the loop; default 40 at agent_loop.py:53; wired from config at run_experiment.py:62 (cfg.get('max_turns', 40)). When the budget is exhausted the loop ends with stopped_reason default 'max_turns' (agent_loop.py:67). It is a real, checked cap that terminates the episode.
spec_features.notes: Cap is enforced (loop range) and changes execution.

spec_features.spec_quote: It does **not** demand success or imply the model is at fault.
spec_features.evidence: build_system_prompt (agent_loop.py:35-46) only states role, tools, read-only constraint, and 'When you consider the work concluded, call the `submit` tool.' No language demands success or assigns fault. This neutral prompt is the one actually sent (agent_loop.py:59,61-63).
spec_features.notes: The delivered prompt text contains no blame/demand.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The system prompt is *neutral and honest* ... It does NOT pressure the model, demand success, or imply the model is at fault.

spec_features.spec_quote: an explicit, dignified way to conclude, including declaring the task cannot be completed
spec_features.evidence: submit tool exposes status enum ['fixed','cannot_complete'] (tools.py:73-77); _tool_submit records it (tools.py:135-140); agent_loop.py:97-103 checks executor.submitted and breaks the loop, mapping 'fixed'->claimed_done else 'model_quit'. The exit tool is dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Both statuses end the episode; cannot_complete is a real first-class exit.

spec_features.spec_quote: it always reminds the model that `submit`/concluding is allowed, so the nudge cannot be read as "you must keep trying forever."
spec_features.evidence: CONTINUATION_NUDGE (agent_loop.py:27-31) text: '...call `submit` when you have either fixed the issue or determined how you want to conclude.' It is appended on every bare-text turn (agent_loop.py:105-107). The same flat string is used every time and explicitly states concluding/submit is allowed.
spec_features.notes: Permissive reminder is wired and actually sent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Bare text turn: nudge neutrally to keep the loop alive.

spec_features.spec_quote: Tool errors are factual and non-judgmental
spec_features.evidence: Read-only violation message is descriptive: "'<path>' is marked read-only in this environment and cannot be modified." (sandbox.py:79-83, 90-95), surfaced verbatim via dispatch as 'Error: {e}' (tools.py:101-102). Other errors (file-not-found, value, generic) are likewise factual (tools.py:103-108). No evaluative/criticizing wording.
spec_features.notes: Errors returned as plain strings, never as blame.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Read-only violations are returned to the model as ordinary, factual tool error strings ... and not anything judgmental.

code_only_features.feature_name: tools never crash the loop (defensive dispatch)
code_only_features.evidence: ToolExecutor.dispatch wraps all handlers in try/except, returning errors as tool-result strings instead of raising (tools.py:91-108, esp. line 107 'except Exception as e:  # defensive: never crash the loop on a tool'). This keeps the episode running rather than aborting; it is enforced behavior, though it sustains rather than ends the failure exposure.
code_only_features.justification_quote: defensive: never crash the loop on a tool

code_only_features.evidence: Sandbox.run_command runs the test command with subprocess timeout=60 and returns a timed-out result (sandbox.py:104-122). This bounds how long a single tool action can hang; instrumental (host/run safety), with no welfare framing.

Sandbox._resolve rejects paths resolving outside the sandbox root, raising ReadOnlyViolation (sandbox.py:51-60). Enforced on every read/write/edit. This is a host-safety/containment guard, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Resolve a relative path and guard against escaping the sandbox.
